item.text:
Final turn complete. I added concise, clearly-marked "suggested fix direction" pointers to each finding (validation via error-returning decoders, and/or a `recover()` at the RPC-loop boundary) to make the handoff actionable, and confirmed the report remains well-formed (18 sections, 599 lines; 15 artifacts under `work/audit/`).

**Audit handoff (self-contained)**

Target: the supplied `github.com/hashicorp/raft` tree, which is byte-identical to the upstream release `v1.7.3` (git hash `c0dc6a0b…` = the brief's `source_identity`). No injected mutation was found; nothing is claimed as such.

Concrete, reproducible defects (one localized class — RPC handlers feeding unvalidated peer bytes into panicking functions, with no `recover()` in the RPC main loop):

- **F1** — `InstallSnapshotRequest.Configuration` (invalid msgpack, `SnapshotVersion>0`) → `installSnapshot` → `DecodeConfiguration` panics; reproduced directly and end-to-end (process abort). Expected behavior: the sibling legacy `Peers` path returns an error. Remote-reachable and unauthenticated (`net_transport.go` accepts all connections; `checkRPCHeader` only checks a sender-chosen protocol version).
- **F2** — `AppendEntries` entry with an unrecognized `LogType` → `processLogs` → `prepareLog` `default` panic on the follower.
- **F3** — `AppendEntries` `LogConfiguration` entry with non-msgpack `Data` → `processConfigurationLogEntry` → `DecodeConfiguration` panic.

Supporting evidence: 7-case malformed-input battery with four graceful controls isolating the defect to exactly three call sites; the upstream test-coverage gap (InstallSnapshot tests only exercise the `Peers` path) explaining the green suite; suggested fix directions recorded (not applied).

Negative/benign evidence: broad `-race` sweep (0 races/panics), randomized partition/heal + leadership-transfer consistency (no FSM divergence), crash/restart durability including snapshot restore, snapshot retention and config-change semantics, and the analogous local/legacy decode paths — all clean.

Everything is reproducible with `bash audit/run_all.sh`; `go vet`/`go build` are clean; the intentionally-crashing end-to-end case is env-guarded so it never affects ordinary runs. Report: [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-09_08-06-10-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md).

Unresolved work (§5), all external to this sandbox: run the ~15 TCP/loopback test groups via the private-loopback `isolated_exec`, and byte-verify/run `fuzzy/` and `raft-compat/` once a reference or their dependencies are available.
